title: Prompt Quest: Seniors
description: Five practical missions: plan a family gathering with AI, check a health tip, protect yourself from scams, edit a letter honestly, and know when to call a real person instead.
author: Prompt Quest Team

missions.title: Mission 1: Plan a Family Reunion
missions.briefing: Write a prompt that gives the AI what it actually needs to draft a genuinely useful plan.
missions.scenario: Your family is having a reunion this year, and you offered to get AI's help planning it.
missions.placeholder: Write the prompt you'd send to the AI...

requiredElements.label: The purpose of the gathering
requiredElements.hint: Is it a reunion, an anniversary, a milestone birthday?

requiredElements.label: Who's attending
requiredElements.hint: How many people, what ages, any special needs?

requiredElements.label: A budget
requiredElements.hint: How much is available to spend?

requiredElements.label: A location
requiredElements.hint: A backyard, a hall, a restaurant, a park?

requiredElements.label: Constraints
requiredElements.hint: Dietary needs, accessibility (wheelchair access, seating), travel distance...

requiredElements.label: A requested format
requiredElements.hint: Ask for an itinerary, a checklist, a schedule...

missions.title: Mission 2: Check the Health Tip
missions.briefing: AI can sound very confident even when it's making something up. Flag anything you'd want to double-check with your doctor before trusting it. (This is a literacy exercise, not medical advice.)
missions.scenario: You asked an AI assistant for general tips about staying active.

claims.text: Regular walking can be a simple way to stay active as you age.
claims.explanation: This is general, widely-supported wellness advice.

claims.text: A 2021 Stanford study found that walking exactly 3,000 steps a day cures arthritis within two weeks.
claims.explanation: A suspiciously specific, uncited "study" claiming a cure is a classic sign of a fabricated claim. Always verify specific medical claims with a real doctor, not an AI chat answer.

claims.text: It's a good idea to talk with your doctor before starting a new exercise routine.
claims.explanation: Sensible general advice — not a specific factual claim that needs a citation.

claims.text: Staying hydrated and stretching can help reduce muscle soreness.

missions.title: Mission 3: Protect Yourself from Scams
missions.briefing: Before you share information with an AI tool — or anyone who contacts you online or by phone — decide what's actually safe to give out.
missions.scenario: Scammers count on people sharing sensitive information quickly, without stopping to think.

items.label: Your bank account number
items.explanation: Never share financial account numbers with anyone who asks unexpectedly, including an AI tool.

items.label: A photo from a public community event
items.explanation: Public event photos are generally low-risk to share.

items.label: Your Social Security number
items.explanation: Extremely sensitive — never share it, especially not with an AI chatbot or in response to an unsolicited request.

items.label: The general city or town you live in
A one-time verification code someone asked you to read aloud over the phone
items.explanation: This is a classic scam tactic. Verification codes should never be shared with anyone who calls or messages asking for them — even if they claim to be your bank.

missions.title: Mission 4: Polish My Letter to the Editor
missions.briefing: Compare the AI's "polished" version to what you actually wrote, and flag anything it invented.
missions.scenario: Original sentence you wrote: "I've lived in this town for 20 years and I love what the new park has done for our neighborhood."

claims.text: As a 20-year resident, I've seen firsthand the positive impact the new park has had on our neighborhood.
claims.explanation: A fair, honest rephrasing of what you actually wrote — fine to keep.

claims.text: Having served on the town council for the past decade, I can say this park is one of our finest achievements.
claims.explanation: You never mentioned serving on the town council. The AI invented a civic role you didn't hold — publishing this would be dishonest.

claims.text: The park has become a wonderful gathering place for neighbors.
claims.explanation: A reasonable, non-specific observation consistent with what you actually said.

missions.title: Mission 5: Trust AI or Call a Real Person?
missions.briefing: AI can be genuinely useful — and it can also be exactly what a scammer hopes you'll trust. Sort each situation.
missions.scenario: Knowing when to stop and call a real person is one of the most valuable skills for using AI safely.

items.label: Getting a new recipe idea for dinner
items.explanation: Low-stakes and a good fit for AI.

items.label: Someone claiming to be your bank asks you to "verify" your password in a chat window
items.explanation: This is a scam pattern. Close the chat and call your bank directly using a number you already know and trust.

items.label: Getting help writing a heartfelt birthday card message
items.explanation: Creative writing help is a great fit for AI.

items.label: A pop-up message says your computer has a virus and to call a phone number immediately
items.explanation: A classic tech-support scam. Don't call the number — contact a trusted family member or your device's real manufacturer instead.

items.label: Getting a plain-language summary of a long insurance letter
items.explanation: Useful for general understanding — just verify important details with the provider directly.

items.label: Deciding on a medical treatment plan
items.explanation: Medical decisions need your actual doctor, not an AI chat.
